accesskeys.title: Keyboard shortcut keys are not used twice
accesskeys.why: If two elements share the same accesskey, the shortcut goes to the wrong place or does nothing.
accesskeys.how_to_fix: Give every accesskey attribute a different letter, or remove accesskey if you do not need it.

area-alt.title: Clickable areas of image maps have text
area-alt.why: Screen reader users hear nothing useful for an image map area with no text, so they cannot tell where it goes.
area-alt.how_to_fix: Add an alt attribute to each <area> with an href. Say where the link goes, like alt="Contact page".

aria-allowed-attr.title: ARIA attributes fit the element's role
aria-allowed-attr.why: Screen readers can ignore or misread ARIA attributes that do not belong to an element's role.
aria-allowed-attr.how_to_fix: Remove the ARIA attributes this role does not support, or change the role to one that supports them.

aria-allowed-role.title: ARIA roles fit the element they are on
aria-allowed-role.why: A role that clashes with the element's normal meaning can confuse screen readers.
aria-allowed-role.how_to_fix: Remove the role, or use an HTML element that already means what you want, like <button> instead of a link with role="button".

aria-braille-equivalent.title: Braille labels also have a normal label
aria-braille-equivalent.why: aria-braillelabel and aria-brailleroledescription only work as extras. People who do not use a braille display need the normal version too.
aria-braille-equivalent.how_to_fix: Keep a normal name (visible text or aria-label) next to aria-braillelabel, and a normal aria-roledescription next to aria-brailleroledescription.

aria-command-name.title: Custom buttons, links and menu items have names
aria-command-name.why: Screen readers announce a control with no name as just "button" or "link", so people cannot tell what it does.
aria-command-name.how_to_fix: Put visible text inside the element, or add aria-label or aria-labelledby.

aria-conditional-attr.title: ARIA attributes are used the way the role expects
aria-conditional-attr.why: Some ARIA attributes only work in certain places. Used elsewhere, they give screen readers wrong or mixed information.
aria-conditional-attr.how_to_fix: Remove the attribute, or move it to an element where it is allowed. The rule page lists the exact cases.

aria-deprecated-role.title: No outdated ARIA roles
aria-deprecated-role.why: Outdated roles may not be supported by screen readers, so the element can lose its meaning.
aria-deprecated-role.how_to_fix: Replace the role with a current one, or with a plain HTML element that means the same thing.

aria-dialog-name.title: Dialogs have a name
aria-dialog-name.why: When a dialog opens, screen readers read its name so people know what it is about.
aria-dialog-name.how_to_fix: Point aria-labelledby at the dialog's heading, or add aria-label.

aria-hidden-body.title: The whole page is not hidden from screen readers
aria-hidden-body.why: aria-hidden="true" on the body hides the entire page from screen readers.

aria-hidden-focus.title: Hidden parts of the page cannot get keyboard focus
aria-hidden-focus.why: Keyboard users can Tab into content that screen readers were told to ignore, and then hear nothing.
aria-hidden-focus.how_to_fix: Remove aria-hidden, or make the controls inside unfocusable (tabindex="-1", disabled, or the inert attribute).

aria-input-field-name.title: Custom input fields have names
aria-input-field-name.why: Screen readers read the field's name to say what to type. Without one, people have to guess.
aria-input-field-name.how_to_fix: Add aria-labelledby pointing at the visible label, or add aria-label.

aria-meter-name.title: Meters have names
aria-meter-name.why: A meter with no name is read as just a number, with no hint of what it measures.
aria-meter-name.how_to_fix: Add aria-label or aria-labelledby that says what the meter shows, like "Battery level".

aria-progressbar-name.title: Progress bars have names
aria-progressbar-name.why: A progress bar with no name is read as just a number, with no hint of what is loading.
aria-progressbar-name.how_to_fix: Add aria-label or aria-labelledby, like "Upload progress".

aria-prohibited-attr.title: No ARIA attributes the element is not allowed to use
aria-prohibited-attr.why: Some roles cannot take a name or certain states. Screen readers may ignore them, so the information is lost.
aria-prohibited-attr.how_to_fix: Remove the attribute, or give the element a role that allows it. For text, put it in the page instead of aria-label.

aria-required-attr.title: Custom controls have the ARIA attributes they need
aria-required-attr.why: Some roles need certain attributes, like aria-checked on a checkbox. Without them, screen readers cannot say the control's state.
aria-required-attr.how_to_fix: Add the missing attributes listed for each element and keep them up to date with script.

aria-required-children.title: ARIA containers hold the right kind of items
aria-required-children.why: Roles like list, menu, or tablist need the right items inside, or screen readers cannot count or move through them.
aria-required-children.how_to_fix: Put the expected child roles inside, like role="tab" inside role="tablist", or remove the container role.

aria-required-parent.title: ARIA items sit inside the right container
aria-required-parent.why: Items like tabs, menu items, or list items only make sense inside their container. Alone, screen readers misreport them.
aria-required-parent.how_to_fix: Wrap the item in its container role, like role="tablist" around role="tab", or remove the item's role.

aria-roledescription.title: Custom role descriptions are on elements with a real role
aria-roledescription.why: aria-roledescription replaces how a role is announced. On an element with no role, it is ignored or confusing.
aria-roledescription.how_to_fix: Only use aria-roledescription on elements that have a role, or remove it.

aria-roles.title: ARIA roles are real roles
aria-roles.why: A misspelled or made-up role is ignored, so the element loses the meaning you meant to give it.
aria-roles.how_to_fix: Fix the spelling, use a role from the ARIA spec, or remove the role.

aria-tab-name.title: Tabs have names
aria-tab-name.why: Screen readers announce a tab with no name as just "tab", so people cannot tell the tabs apart.
aria-tab-name.how_to_fix: Put visible text in each tab, or add aria-label.

aria-text.title: Text marked role="text" has nothing focusable inside
aria-text.why: role="text" flattens everything inside into plain text, so a link or button inside it loses its meaning.
aria-text.how_to_fix: Remove role="text", or move the focusable element outside of it.

aria-toggle-field-name.title: Custom checkboxes, switches and toggles have names
aria-toggle-field-name.why: Screen readers announce a toggle with no name as just "checkbox" or "switch", so people do not know what it changes.
aria-toggle-field-name.how_to_fix: Put visible text inside, or add aria-label or aria-labelledby.

aria-tooltip-name.title: Tooltips have text
aria-tooltip-name.why: An empty tooltip gives screen reader users nothing to read.
aria-tooltip-name.how_to_fix: Put text inside the element with role="tooltip", or add aria-label.

aria-treeitem-name.title: Tree items have names
aria-treeitem-name.why: Screen readers announce a tree item with no name as just "tree item", so people cannot find their way.
aria-treeitem-name.how_to_fix: Put visible text in each tree item, or add aria-label.

aria-valid-attr-value.title: ARIA attributes have valid values
aria-valid-attr-value.why: An attribute with a wrong value, like aria-expanded="yes", is ignored, so screen readers get the wrong state.
aria-valid-attr-value.how_to_fix: Use an allowed value, like "true" or "false", and make sure ID references point at elements that exist.

aria-valid-attr.title: ARIA attribute names are spelled right
aria-valid-attr.why: A misspelled ARIA attribute is ignored, so the information it should carry is lost.
aria-valid-attr.how_to_fix: Fix the spelling, like aria-labelledby (two l's), or remove the attribute.

audio-caption.title: Audio has a text version
audio-caption.why: Deaf and hard of hearing people need words for what is said in audio.
audio-caption.how_to_fix: Add a transcript near the audio player, or a captions track.

autocomplete-valid.title: Autocomplete values are correct
autocomplete-valid.why: The right autocomplete value lets browsers fill in personal details, which helps people with memory or motor disabilities.
autocomplete-valid.how_to_fix: Use a value from the HTML list, like autocomplete="email" or "given-name", or remove a wrong one.

avoid-inline-spacing.title: Text spacing can be changed by the reader
avoid-inline-spacing.why: Some people need more space between letters, words, or lines to read. Inline styles with !important block their own settings.
avoid-inline-spacing.how_to_fix: Remove !important from inline letter-spacing, word-spacing, and line-height, or move those styles into your style sheet.

blink.title: No blinking text
blink.why: Blinking text is hard to read and distracting, and some people cannot focus on the page while it moves.
blink.how_to_fix: Remove the <blink> element. If something needs attention, use color, weight, or a heading instead.

button-name.title: Buttons have names that screen readers can read
button-name.why: Screen readers announce a button with no name as just "button", so people do not know what it does.
button-name.how_to_fix: Put text inside the button. For icon buttons, add aria-label, or visually hidden text inside the button.

bypass.title: There is a way to skip to the main content
bypass.why: Keyboard and screen reader users otherwise have to go through the whole menu on every page.
bypass.how_to_fix: Add a "Skip to main content" link at the top, wrap the main content in <main>, or use headings at the start of each section.

color-contrast.title: Text stands out clearly from its background
color-contrast.why: Faint text is hard or impossible to read for people with low vision or color blindness, and for anyone in bright light.
color-contrast.how_to_fix: Make the text darker or the background lighter, or the other way around. Normal text needs at least 4.5 to 1, large text at least 3 to 1.

css-orientation-lock.title: The page works in both portrait and landscape
css-orientation-lock.why: Some people have their device mounted in one position and cannot turn it.
css-orientation-lock.how_to_fix: Do not use CSS to force one orientation. Let the layout adapt to both.

definition-list.title: Definition lists are built correctly
definition-list.why: Screen readers rely on the <dl>, <dt>, <dd> structure to read terms and their meanings together.
definition-list.how_to_fix: Inside a <dl>, only use groups of <dt> and <dd> (optionally wrapped in <div>). Move anything else out.

dlitem.title: Terms and definitions are inside a definition list
dlitem.why: A <dt> or <dd> on its own does not tell screen readers it belongs to a list of terms.

document-title.title: The page has a title
document-title.why: The title is the first thing screen readers read, and it names the browser tab.
document-title.how_to_fix: Add a <title> in the <head> that says what this page is, like "Contact us: Example Shop".

duplicate-id-aria.title: IDs used by labels and ARIA are unique
duplicate-id-aria.why: If two elements share an ID, a label or aria-labelledby can point at the wrong one.
duplicate-id-aria.how_to_fix: Give each element a different ID, and update the label or ARIA attribute that points at it.

empty-heading.title: Headings are not empty
empty-heading.why: Screen reader users jump between headings. An empty one is announced as "heading" with nothing after it.
empty-heading.how_to_fix: Put text in the heading, or remove the heading element if it is only used for spacing or style.

empty-table-header.title: Table headers have text
empty-table-header.why: Screen readers read the header with each cell. An empty header gives no context.
empty-table-header.how_to_fix: Put text in every <th>. If a column truly has no header, use <td> instead.

focus-order-semantics.title: Things you can Tab to have a role
focus-order-semantics.why: If you can Tab to something, screen readers need to know what it is, like a button or a link.
focus-order-semantics.how_to_fix: Use a real <button> or <a>, or add a fitting role to the element that has tabindex.

form-field-multiple-labels.title: Each form field has one label
form-field-multiple-labels.why: When a field has several labels, screen readers may read only one, or read them in a confusing way.
form-field-multiple-labels.how_to_fix: Keep one <label> per field. Put extra hints in text linked with aria-describedby.

frame-focusable-content.title: Frames with controls can be reached by keyboard
frame-focusable-content.why: tabindex="-1" on a frame stops keyboard users from reaching the buttons and links inside it.

frame-tested.title: Some frames could not be checked
frame-tested.why: The scan could not get into these frames, so problems inside them are not in the results.
frame-tested.how_to_fix: Open the frame's address on its own and scan it there, or check it by hand.

frame-title-unique.title: Each frame has a different title
frame-title-unique.why: Screen reader users pick frames by title. If titles repeat, they cannot tell them apart.
frame-title-unique.how_to_fix: Give each <iframe> a title that says what is inside it.

frame-title.title: Frames have a title
frame-title.why: Screen readers read the title so people know what the frame contains before going in.
frame-title.how_to_fix: Add a title attribute to each <iframe>, like title="Map of our office".

heading-order.title: Heading levels go down one step at a time
heading-order.why: Skipping levels, like h2 straight to h4, makes screen reader users think they missed something.
heading-order.how_to_fix: Use the next level down for sub-sections. Change the size with CSS, not by picking a different heading level.

hidden-content.title: Hidden content was not checked
hidden-content.why: The scan cannot check content that is hidden right now, like closed menus or tabs.
hidden-content.how_to_fix: Open the hidden parts of the page, then scan again.

html-has-lang.title: The page says which language it is in
html-has-lang.why: Screen readers use the page language to pick the right voice and pronunciation.
html-has-lang.how_to_fix: Add a lang attribute to the <html> element, like <html lang="en">.

html-lang-valid.title: The page says which language it is in
html-lang-valid.why: Screen readers use the page language to pick the right voice. A wrong code means a wrong voice.
html-lang-valid.how_to_fix: Use a real language code in <html lang>, like "en", "en-GB", or "fr".

html-xml-lang-mismatch.title: The two page language settings agree
html-xml-lang-mismatch.why: When lang and xml:lang say different languages, screen readers may pick the wrong voice.
html-xml-lang-mismatch.how_to_fix: Make lang and xml:lang on <html> match, or remove xml:lang.

image-alt.title: Images have a text description
image-alt.why: Screen readers read the description out loud instead of showing the image. Without one, people hear the file name or nothing.
image-alt.how_to_fix: Add an alt attribute to every that says what the image shows. For decoration only, use alt="".

image-redundant-alt.title: Image text does not repeat the text next to it
image-redundant-alt.why: Screen reader users hear the same words twice in a row.
image-redundant-alt.how_to_fix: If the text next to the image already says it, use alt="". Otherwise make the alt add something new.

input-button-name.title: Input buttons have text
input-button-name.why: Screen readers announce an input button with no text as just "button".
input-button-name.how_to_fix: Add a value attribute, like <input type="submit" value="Send">, or add aria-label.

input-image-alt.title: Image buttons have text
input-image-alt.why: A button made from an image has no text unless you add it, so screen readers cannot say what it does.
input-image-alt.how_to_fix: Add an alt attribute to <input type="image"> that says what the button does, like alt="Search".

label-content-name-mismatch.title: A control's name includes its visible text
label-content-name-mismatch.why: Voice control users say what they see. If the hidden name is different, saying the visible words does nothing.
label-content-name-mismatch.how_to_fix: Make aria-label start with, or contain, the visible text. Or remove aria-label and use the visible text as the name.

label-title-only.title: Form fields have a visible label
label-title-only.why: A label that only appears as a tooltip is hidden from many people, including touch and keyboard users.
label-title-only.how_to_fix: Add a visible <label> for the field. Keep title only for extra hints, if at all.

label.title: Form fields have labels
label.why: Screen readers read a field's label to say what to type. Without one, people hear "edit text" and have to guess.
label.how_to_fix: Add a <label for="field-id"> for every field, or wrap the field in the label.

landmark-banner-is-top-level.title: The page header is not inside another region
landmark-banner-is-top-level.why: Screen reader users jump to the header as a main part of the page. Nested inside something else, it is harder to find.
landmark-banner-is-top-level.how_to_fix: Move the site <header> (or role="banner") so it is not inside <main>, <nav>, <aside>, or another region.

landmark-complementary-is-top-level.title: Side content is not inside another region
landmark-complementary-is-top-level.why: Screen reader users jump to <aside> regions directly. Nested, they are harder to find.
landmark-complementary-is-top-level.how_to_fix: Move the <aside> (or role="complementary") out of other regions, so it sits next to <main>.

landmark-contentinfo-is-top-level.title: The page footer is not inside another region
landmark-contentinfo-is-top-level.why: Screen reader users jump to the footer as a main part of the page. Nested inside something else, it is harder to find.
landmark-contentinfo-is-top-level.how_to_fix: Move the site <footer> (or role="contentinfo") so it is not inside <main> or another region.

landmark-main-is-top-level.title: The main content is not inside another region
landmark-main-is-top-level.why: Screen reader users jump straight to <main>. Nested inside something else, it is harder to find.
landmark-main-is-top-level.how_to_fix: Move <main> so it is not inside <header>, <nav>, <aside>, or <footer>.

landmark-no-duplicate-banner.title: The page has only one site header
landmark-no-duplicate-banner.why: Two site headers make it unclear which one is the real top of the page.
landmark-no-duplicate-banner.how_to_fix: Keep one top-level <header> for the site. Headers inside <article> or <section> are fine.

landmark-no-duplicate-contentinfo.title: The page has only one site footer
landmark-no-duplicate-contentinfo.why: Two site footers make it unclear which one is the real end of the page.
landmark-no-duplicate-contentinfo.how_to_fix: Keep one top-level <footer> for the site. Footers inside <article> or <section> are fine.

landmark-no-duplicate-main.title: The page has only one main area
landmark-no-duplicate-main.why: Screen reader users jump to the main content. With two, they may land in the wrong place.
landmark-no-duplicate-main.how_to_fix: Use one visible <main> element per page.

landmark-one-main.title: The page marks its main content
landmark-one-main.why: Screen reader users jump straight to the main content. Without a <main>, they have to search for it.
landmark-one-main.how_to_fix: Wrap the main content of the page in a <main> element.

landmark-unique.title: Page regions of the same kind have different names
landmark-unique.why: If a page has two <nav> regions with no names, screen reader users cannot tell them apart.
landmark-unique.how_to_fix: Give each one a label, like <nav aria-label="Main"> and <nav aria-label="Footer">.

link-in-text-block.title: Links in text stand out without relying on color
link-in-text-block.why: People who cannot see the color difference cannot find links that differ from text only by color.
link-in-text-block.how_to_fix: Underline links in text, or give them another visible difference besides color.

link-name.title: Links have text that screen readers can read
link-name.why: Screen readers read the link text to say where a link goes. A link with no text is read as just "link".
link-name.how_to_fix: Put text inside the link. For icon or image links, add alt text to the image or aria-label to the link.

list.title: Lists only contain list items
list.why: Screen readers count the items and let people move through them. Other elements directly inside break that.
list.how_to_fix: Inside <ul> and <ol>, only put <li> elements. Put other content inside an <li>.

listitem.title: List items are inside a list
listitem.why: An <li> on its own is not read as part of a list.

marquee.title: No scrolling marquee text
marquee.why: Moving text is hard to read and distracting, and it cannot be paused.
marquee.how_to_fix: Remove the <marquee> element and show the text normally.

meta-refresh.title: The page does not reload or redirect on a timer
meta-refresh.why: A timed reload can move people away before they finish reading, and it resets screen reader position.
meta-refresh.how_to_fix: Remove the <meta http-equiv="refresh"> timer. Redirect on the server instead, or let people choose when to reload.

meta-viewport-large.title: People can zoom in a lot on mobile
meta-viewport-large.why: People with low vision often need to zoom far in on phones.
meta-viewport-large.how_to_fix: In the viewport meta tag, remove maximum-scale or set it to 5 or more.

meta-viewport.title: People can zoom in on mobile
meta-viewport.why: Blocking zoom stops people with low vision from making text bigger.
meta-viewport.how_to_fix: In the viewport meta tag, remove user-scalable=no and any maximum-scale below 2.

nested-interactive.title: Controls are not put inside other controls
nested-interactive.why: A button inside a link (or the other way around) is read wrong by screen readers, and the inner one may not work by keyboard.
nested-interactive.how_to_fix: Move the inner control out, so each button or link stands on its own.

no-autoplay-audio.title: Sound does not play on its own
no-autoplay-audio.why: Sound that starts by itself covers up the screen reader voice.
no-autoplay-audio.how_to_fix: Do not autoplay sound. If you must, stop it within 3 seconds or give a control to pause or mute it.

object-alt.title: Embedded objects have text
object-alt.why: Screen readers cannot describe an <object> with no text alternative.
object-alt.how_to_fix: Add aria-label or a title to the <object>, or put a text description inside it.

p-as-heading.title: Bold text is not used as a fake heading
p-as-heading.why: Text that only looks like a heading does not show up when screen reader users jump between headings.
p-as-heading.how_to_fix: If it is a heading, use <h2>, <h3>, and so on, and style it with CSS.

page-has-heading-one.title: The page has a main heading
page-has-heading-one.why: Screen reader users often jump to the h1 first to learn what the page is about.
page-has-heading-one.how_to_fix: Add one <h1> that says what the page is about.

presentation-role-conflict.title: Elements marked as decoration really are ignored
presentation-role-conflict.why: If an element marked role="none" can still get focus or has ARIA, browsers expose it anyway, which confuses screen readers.
presentation-role-conflict.how_to_fix: Remove role="none" or role="presentation", or remove the tabindex and global ARIA attributes from that element.

region.title: All content is inside a page region
region.why: Screen reader users move around by regions like header, main, and footer. Content outside them is easy to miss.

role-img-alt.title: Elements marked as images have text
role-img-alt.why: An element with role="img" and no text is read as just "image".
role-img-alt.how_to_fix: Add aria-label or aria-labelledby that describes the image.

scope-attr-valid.title: Table header scope is used correctly
scope-attr-valid.why: A wrong scope can make screen readers link cells to the wrong header.
scope-attr-valid.how_to_fix: Only use scope on <th>, with the value row, col, rowgroup, or colgroup.

scrollable-region-focusable.title: Scrolling areas can be scrolled with the keyboard
scrollable-region-focusable.why: If a scrolling box cannot get focus, keyboard users cannot scroll it to see the rest.
scrollable-region-focusable.how_to_fix: Add tabindex="0" and a label to the scrolling box, or make sure it contains something focusable.

select-name.title: Dropdowns have labels
select-name.why: Screen readers read the label to say what the dropdown is for.
select-name.how_to_fix: Add a <label for="id"> for every <select>, or add aria-label.

server-side-image-map.title: No server-side image maps
server-side-image-map.why: Server-side image maps only work with a mouse click, so keyboard users cannot use them.
server-side-image-map.how_to_fix: Use separate links, or a client-side map with <map> and <area> elements.

skip-link.title: Skip links lead somewhere
skip-link.why: A skip link whose target is missing does nothing, so keyboard users stay stuck at the top.
skip-link.how_to_fix: Make the link's #target match an element ID on the page, like <main id="main">.

summary-name.title: Expand and collapse controls have text
summary-name.why: A <summary> with no text is read as just "button" or "disclosure", so people do not know what it opens.

svg-img-alt.title: Images made with SVG have text
svg-img-alt.why: An SVG marked as an image with no text is read as just "image".
svg-img-alt.how_to_fix: Add a <title> as the first child of the SVG, or aria-label on the <svg>.

tabindex.title: No tabindex values above zero
tabindex.why: A tabindex above zero changes the Tab order, so focus jumps around the page in a confusing way.
tabindex.how_to_fix: Use tabindex="0" or remove tabindex, and put elements in the right order in the HTML.

table-duplicate-name.title: A table's caption and summary say different things
table-duplicate-name.why: Screen readers read both, so the same words are heard twice.
table-duplicate-name.how_to_fix: Make the summary add something the caption does not say, or remove the summary.

table-fake-caption.title: Table titles use a caption, not a table cell
table-fake-caption.why: A title put in a cell is read as data, not as the table's name.
table-fake-caption.how_to_fix: Move the title into a <caption> element right after <table>.

target-size.title: Buttons and links are big enough to tap
target-size.why: Small targets close together are hard to hit for people with shaky hands or on touch screens.
target-size.how_to_fix: Make each target at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels, or leave enough space around small ones so they do not crowd each other.

td-has-header.title: Cells in large tables have headers
td-has-header.why: In big tables, screen reader users need headers read with each cell to know what the number means.
td-has-header.how_to_fix: Use <th> for row and column headers, with scope="col" or scope="row".

td-headers-attr.title: Table cells point at real headers
td-headers-attr.why: If a headers attribute points at a missing ID, screen readers cannot say which header goes with the cell.
td-headers-attr.how_to_fix: Make each ID in the headers attribute match a <th> in the same table.

th-has-data-cells.title: Table headers have cells under them
th-has-data-cells.why: A header with no cells confuses screen reader users who move through the table.
th-has-data-cells.how_to_fix: Remove empty header rows or columns, or make sure each <th> has data cells.

valid-lang.title: Language changes use real language codes
valid-lang.why: Screen readers switch voice for parts in another language. A wrong code means a wrong voice.
valid-lang.how_to_fix: Use a real code on the lang attribute, like lang="es" for Spanish.

video-caption.title: Videos have captions
video-caption.why: Deaf and hard of hearing people need captions to follow speech and sounds in a video.
video-caption.how_to_fix: Add a <track kind="captions"> to the <video>, with a captions file.
